questions.title: Directed Cycle Detection
questions.description:
The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(int V, int g[][MAXV])

It must return 1 when the directed graph contains a directed cycle, 0 otherwise. Use DFS with three colors per node (0 = unvisited, 1 = on the current recursion stack, 2 = finished): reaching a color-1 node again is a back edge, i.e. a cycle.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E directed edge lines.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)

questions.title: Self-Loop Scan
questions.description:

Implement only this function:

    int has_self_loop(int V, int g[][MAXV])

It must return 1 when any g[i][i] equals 1 (a self-loop is a 1-cycle), 0 otherwise. Just scan the diagonal.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E directed edge lines.

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*V

questions.title: Total Cable Weight
questions.description:
The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected WEIGHTED adjacency matrix w from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each "u v wt", w[u][v] = w[v][u] = wt with wt >= 1; 0 means no edge).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int total_weight(int V, int w[][MAXV])

It must return the sum of all cable weights in the network — each undirected edge once (scan one triangle of the symmetric matrix, or halve the full sum).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines "u v wt".

Output Format:
One line with the total weight.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)/2, 1 <= wt <= 1000000000

questions.title: Build System Cycle Alert
questions.description:
A build system cannot schedule compile jobs when the dependency graph between them is cyclic. Detect it with DFS colors. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(int V, int g[][MAXV])

It must return 1 when the dependency digraph has a directed cycle, 0 otherwise (0 = unvisited, 1 = on the recursion stack, 2 = finished; a back edge to a color-1 node is a cycle).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E dependency lines "u v" (u must build before v).

Output Format:
One line with 1 (cyclic — refuse to build) or 0 (schedulable).

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)

Input Format:

Output Format:

questions.title: Friend Circle Count
questions.description:
A social app merges profiles into FRIEND CIRCLES with a union-find: process friendships in order, uniting each pair's sets, then count the distinct group leaders left. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement these two functions:

    int uf_find(int *parent, int x)
    void uf_union(int *parent, int a, int b)

uf_find must follow parent[] links until it reaches a root (parent[x] == x) and return it. uf_union must unite the sets of a and b: attach the root of a UNDER the root of b (only when the roots differ). The harness reads V people and E friendships, unions each pair, then counts roots.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E friendship lines "a b" (0-indexed people).

Output Format:
One line with the number of friend circles.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 2000

questions.title: Merge Conflict Loop
questions.description:
A version-control server detects cherry-pick loops: a cycle in the rebase-request digraph means two branches keep requesting each other. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int has_cycle(int V, int g[][MAXV])

It must return 1 when the digraph contains a directed cycle, 0 otherwise — DFS with colors (0 unvisited, 1 on stack, 2 finished).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E request lines "u v".

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)

questions.title: Union-Find Friend Queries
questions.description:
A support bot merges user accounts into groups with union-find, then answers connectivity questions. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement these two functions:

    int uf_find(int *parent, int x)
    void uf_union(int *parent, int a, int b)

uf_find must chase parent[] links until a root (parent[x] == x) and return it. uf_union must attach the root of a UNDER the root of b (skip when both share a root). The harness reads V users and E merges, applies each with uf_union, then reads q queries; for each pair it prints "yes" when uf_find matches, else "no".

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E merge lines "a b". Line 3: q. Then q query lines "a b".

Output Format:
q lines, each "yes" (same group) or "no" (different groups).

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E, q <= 2000

questions.title: Undirected Cycle via Union-Find
questions.description:
A cabling crew detects redundant links: adding an edge whose endpoints are ALREADY in the same union-find set creates a cycle in the undirected network. The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int uf_has_cycle(int V, int E, int eu[], int ev[])

It must process edges in order with an internal union-find (parent[i] = i initially): for each edge, when find(eu) == find(ev) the graph has a cycle — return 1 immediately; otherwise union the roots (attach a's root under b's root). Return 0 after all edges.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E edge lines "u v" (0-indexed, undirected).

Output Format:
One line with 1 or 0.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= 2000

questions.title: Source Tasks in Order
questions.description:
A planner lists every dependency-free task (indegree 0) in ascending id — the tasks that can start immediately in any topological schedule. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void sources_fill(int V, int g[][MAXV], int out[], int *outn)

It must fill out[] with all zero-indegree node indices in ASCENDING order and set *outn to the count. (The input is a DAG, so at least one source exists.) The harness prints them space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E dependency lines "u v".

Output Format:
One line with the source ids space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)

questions.title: Minimum Spanning Cable
questions.description:
A fiber rollout must connect every site with minimum total cable — the MST weight of the weighted network. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected WEIGHTED adjacency matrix w from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each "u v wt", w[u][v] = w[v][u] = wt with wt >= 1; 0 means no edge).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int mst_weight(int V, int w[][MAXV])

It must return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree (the network is connected). Use Prim's algorithm: start with node 0 in the tree; at every step add the cheapest edge leaving the tree; sum the added weights.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines "u v wt".

Output Format:
One line with the MST total weight.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, V-1 <= E <= V*(V-1)/2, 1 <= wt <= 1000000000, graph connected

questions.title: Minimum Hop Route
questions.description:
A packet router reports the fewest hops from source to destination in a DIRECTED graph (each edge costs 1 hop; -1 when the destination is unreachable). The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int min_hops(int V, int g[][MAXV], int src, int dst)

It must BFS over OUTGOING edges from src (ascending-index scans) and return the minimum number of edges on a directed path to dst, or -1 when unreachable (src == dst costs 0).

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E directed edge lines. Last line: src and dst.

Output Format:
One line with the hop count or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1), 0 <= src, dst < V

questions.title: Task Order Fill
questions.description:
A scheduler emits a full topological order of a DAG with Kahn's algorithm, always picking the SMALLEST-indexed available task. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds a DIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a directed edge "u v" meaning u -> v).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    void topo_fill(int V, int g[][MAXV], int out[])

It must fill out[] with a topological order of the input DAG (line 1 gives a DAG; edges u -> v): first compute each node's indegree, then repeat V times — pick the SMALLEST-indexed node whose indegree is 0 and that is not yet output, append it, and decrement the indegree of everything it points to. The harness prints the order space-separated.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E dependency lines "u v" (u before v).

Output Format:
One line with the topological order, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1), input is a DAG

questions.title: Fastest Delivery Route
questions.description:
A courier network must report the shortest travel time from depot 0 to depot V-1 over its weighted links — Dijkstra on a small matrix. The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an undirected WEIGHTED adjacency matrix w from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each "u v wt", w[u][v] = w[v][u] = wt with wt >= 1; 0 means no edge).

The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int dijkstra_dist(int V, int w[][MAXV])

It must return the minimum total weight of a path from node 0 to node V-1, or -1 when V-1 is unreachable. Use Dijkstra: dist[0] = 0; repeatedly finalize the unvisited node with the smallest finite dist, relaxing all its edges; dist[v] = -1 marks unknown.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E lines "u v wt".

Output Format:
One line with the shortest travel time or -1.

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)/2, 1 <= wt <= 1000000000

questions.title: Island Count Survey
questions.description:
A satellite survey counts ISLANDS in a sea/land map: land cells are '1', water '0'; islands are groups of land cells connected horizontally or vertically (NOT diagonally). The scaffold defines MAXG as 12 and reads the grid into char g[][MAXG] (line 1: R C; then R map rows of C characters). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int num_islands(int R, int C, char g[][MAXG])

It must return the number of islands. Scan every cell; when you find an unvisited '1', count one island and FLOOD-FILL (DFS) it — mark every connected land cell by overwriting it with '0' so it is never counted twice.

Input Format:
Line 1: R C. Then R lines, each a string of C characters ('0'/'1').

Output Format:
One line with the island count.

Constraints:
1 <= R, C <= 10, cells are '0' or '1'

questions.title: Two-Team Assignment
questions.description:
A tournament scheduler splits players into two teams so that EVERY rivalry edge joins players of DIFFERENT teams — exactly a bipartiteness test via 2-coloring (possible iff the graph has no odd cycle). The scaffold defines MAXV as 50 and builds an UNDIRECTED adjacency matrix g from the input (line 1: V E; then E lines, each a rivalry "u v", g[u][v] = g[v][u] = 1). The program scaffolding (includes and main) is already set up for you.

Implement only this function:

    int is_bipartite(int V, int g[][MAXV])

It must return 1 when a 2-coloring exists, 0 otherwise. BFS each unvisited component: color the start 0; when exploring an edge, an uncolored neighbor gets the opposite color and joins the queue, while a same-colored neighbor proves the graph is NOT bipartite.

Input Format:
Line 1: V E. Then E rivalry lines "u v".

Output Format:
One line with 1 (assignable) or 0 (impossible).

Constraints:
1 <= V <= 50, 0 <= E <= V*(V-1)/2
